correctness.rationale: In S0 each of the 2s output fields costs 2|v|+2 bits; non-self-loop target fields can only increase cost. For total stored output L and input length k, n<=kL, so every description costs at least 4s+2L+k>=4+2 sqrt(2n). One state with outputs 0^a and the empty word, fed 0^(2a), costs 2a+4+2a and produces 0^(2a^2). Equality in the real bound forces 2n to be a square because the cost is integral; the even square root is 2a. This verifies the result for every n>=1, including descriptions with unreachable states. Inspected the encoding source and frozen VERIFICATION.md; no enumeration is needed.

evidence: Write M for the longest transition output length and k for the input length. The prior proof explicitly gives Mk>=n and cost>=2M+k. The same prior encoding charges two delimiter bits per field and at least two fields, so cost>=2M+k+4 without requiring any further bound. Minimizing 2M+k at fixed Mk gives k=2M and equality in Mk>=n requires n=2M^2. The prior one-state witness has a block-output self-loop and a second loop for padding; on the exact product use only the first loop and set the unused output empty, achieving the equality cost.

No new constraint on an optimal transducer, independent lower-bound mechanism or distinct construction is needed.
